summary: Renjo Akamatsu (1841–1919) was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Chō Sanshū and held a post at Ryukoku University.

Renshan Yang (1837–1911) was a Buddhist studies scholar who founded the Jinling Scriptural Press (1897), Jetavana Hermitage (1908), and Buddhist Research Society (1910), serving as the society's head. He taught Jian Ouyang, Bohua Gui, Taiyan Zhang, Tan Sitong, and Taixu.
René Daumal (1908–1944) was an author and scholar in indology and philosophy. He studied at the Lycée Henri-IV from circa 1925 to 1927 and at the Sorbonne from circa 1927 to 1929.

René Fohalle (1899–1984) was a linguist and indologist who studied at the University of Liège, under Joseph Mansion, and under Antoine Meillet and Émile Benveniste. He succeeded Mansion and served as Ordinary Professor at the University of Liège from 1929 to 1969.
René Gothóni (born 1950) works in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Helsinki from circa 1969 to 1975, where he became emeritus professor in 2016.

René Grousset (1885–1952) specialized in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and sinology after studying at the University of Montpellier. He directed the Musée Cernuschi (1933) and held posts at the Guimet Museum, École du Louvre, INALCO, and Musée du Louvre.

René Guénon (1886–1951) was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied at École Polytechnique, the University of Paris, and the Sorbonne, and studied under Sylvain Lévi circa 1915 to 1921.

René de Nebesky-Wojkowitz (1923–1959) worked in Tibetology, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Charles University, Humboldt University, SOAS, LSE, and the University of Vienna under scholars including Bleichsteiner and Tucci, later serving as Privatdozent at Vienna and at Weltmuseum Wien.
Reo Fortune (1903–1979) studied at Victoria University of Wellington and the University of Cambridge under Thomas Callan Hodson. He held a post at the University of Cambridge from circa 1947 to 1970.

Reuben Burrow (1747–1792) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He served as assistant astronomer and schoolmaster at the Royal Observatory, Greenwich (~1770–1771), arithmetical teacher at the Tower of London (~1775–1782), and was a member of The Asiatic Society (~1784–1792).

Reuven Kahane (1931–2003) was a scholar of Indology and sociology who earned his Ph.D. under Neil Smelser at UC Berkeley. From circa 1970 to 2000, he was a lecturer and then Professor of Sociology and Anthropology at Hebrew University of Jerusalem.

Revilo Pendleton Oliver (1908–1994) worked in Indology and classics. He completed his Ph.D. under William Abbott Oldfather at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, where he taught from 1945 and served as Professor of Classics from 1953 to 1977.
Rewa Prasad Dwivedi (1935–2021) was an Indology scholar who studied at Banaras Hindu University (~1955–1960). He later served there as Head of Sahityavidya from circa 1977 to 1995.

Rewata Dhamma (1929–2004) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed a BA, MA, and PhD at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University between 1956 and 1967, and also earned a doctorate at Banaras Hindu University (1956–1967).

Ria Kloppenborg (1945–2003) studied Indology and religious studies at Leiden and Utrecht, completing her Ph.D. under Jan Gonda. She held posts at Utrecht University (1970–1975, 1988 as Professor of History of Religions) and the University of Groningen (1979–1988).

Richa Negi completed an M.Tech at Kurukshetra University (1994) and a Ph.D. at MNNIT Allahabad (2013). Working in Indology, history, and archaeology, she was attested as Head of Department at the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts in 2026.

Richard A. Hutch (born 1945) is a religious studies scholar who studied at Gettysburg College, Yale Divinity School, and the University of Chicago. He held academic posts at Southern Illinois University (~1974–1978) and the University of Queensland (~1978–2010).

Richard B. Mahoney earned his MA under Paul Harrison at the University of Canterbury by 2002. Working in Buddhist studies and computational fields, he was attested in 2019 holding the Singhmar Chair in Classical Indian Society and Polity at the University of Alberta.

Richard B. Martin is an Indology and Tibetology scholar. He held positions at the University of Virginia, where he was attested as a professor from 1983 to 1991 and as a South Asian bibliographer in 2003.

Richard Baker (born 1936) is a Buddhist studies teacher who studied under Shunryu Suzuki and at UC Berkeley, Wisconsin, Minnesota, Colorado, and Harvard. He founded the Dharma Sangha and the San Francisco Zen Center, where he was abbot from 1971 to 1984.
